title: Bench run manifest
description: Immutable record of one benchmark run. Append-only: a correction is a new run, not an edit. Exists so cost is never conflated with quality.

regime.description: the coarse class. Kept at three values on purpose: widening it would change what an existing field means across already-recorded runs. run_regime.py DERIVES it from the toggles (raw = no decomposition, no review, no council; native = a lead fans out with no protocol artifacts; protocol = everything else, ablated or not) and puts the config's own label in regime_name.

regime_name.description: the regime config's own label, e.g. 'protocol-full', 'no-council'. The named ablations of bench/regimes/README.md live here; `regime` stays the coarse class.

toggles.description: the mechanism vector this run was configured with — the authoritative record of which parts of the protocol were on. `ablation` names at most one removed mechanism and is null whenever zero or several are off, so this is the field to read.

git_revision.description: sha of the org protocol used

injected_event.description: null for no-event runs (all v0.9 runs are null)

ablation.description: which single protocol component was disabled, or null. Null means EITHER nothing was disabled (protocol-full) OR several were (raw, native) — in both of those cases one name would be a lie, so read `toggles` for the truth. 'senior_review' is the name this vocabulary already used for the `review` toggle.

models.description: role -> model id, so the model mix is on the record

seat_invocations.description: foreign ask-agent seat invocations. Kept separate from model_calls (Claude assistant turns) because one codex session and one Claude turn are not the same unit and adding them yields a number that means nothing.

escaped_defects.description: found by the external suite AFTER the org called it done

grading_stages.description: the frozen exam run more than once: 'after_build' (before any review touched the code) and 'final'. The difference is what the review ladder cost or bought in graded conformance, and it is what grading.fix_introduced_regressions is computed from. `grading` above always mirrors the FINAL stage.

review_steps.description: PRIMARY METRIC: bugs caught, broken down by review step ('native', 'council', 'lead', 'cto'), and within a step by round. Each entry: {ran, skipped_reason, rounds[], totals{critical,important,minor,unknown,total,rounds,rounds_unparsed}, fix_rounds_applied}. A round whose findings block did not parse contributes to rounds_unparsed and to NO severity count — 'could not parse' is never recorded as 'zero findings'. Per-round detail is descriptive; the top-level shape is the contract.

rounds.description: one entry per review round, in order. Deliberately unconstrained: the per-round detail is descriptive and differs by step, while the step's `totals` are the contract. A claude round carries round, model, reviewed_sha, had_checkout, inlined_source_complete, partial, proc, parse_ok, parse_error, counts, findings; a council round carries round, reviewed_sha, seats, parse_ok, partial, source_complete, counts, seats_expected/filled/empty, union_note. `partial` means the reviewer saw less than the build: for a council seat that is a missing seat or incomplete inlined source, for a claude reviewer it is a missing checkout (it can read past a truncated inlining, a council seat cannot).

escaped_defects.description: THE ROBUSTNESS YARDSTICK: a post-hoc cross-provider audit (codex + agy) of the FINAL server, run identically for every regime from a deliberately regime-independent prompt so the counts are comparable across arms. `critical_important` is the headline number and is mirrored into grading.escaped_defects. Counts are the SUM across seats with no semantic deduplication — two seats reporting one defect count twice. Null, not zero, when no seat returned a parsable block.

tokens_by_phase.description: token usage per phase: 'build', 'review:<step>', 'audit'. Each entry carries its own `source` and an `estimated` flag — a `claude -p` phase is measured from the result event's per-session modelUsage aggregate; a foreign ask-agent seat reports no usage at all and is estimated at characters/4. Never compare an estimated figure with a measured one without saying so.

wall_clock_by_phase.description: seconds per phase, measured by the harness around each subprocess

standup.description: the situational-awareness loop's own record: observes run, stalls flagged, redirects sent

crystal.description: the speculative-merge loop's record: checks run, how many reported a conflict, and the conflicting stanzas

failures.description: every failure the run hit, in order, each {phase, kind, detail, at}. A run that finished with an empty server and a red exam still writes a complete manifest — a run directory that is only complete on the happy path is not evidence.

harness.description: how the measurement itself was made: the script, the pristine framework worktree, sha256 of every pinned input (spec, exam, runbook, doctrine), whether the run tree's copy of the exam was modified, and the stated cost-bucketing and token-source rules. `accepted_limitations` records the study limitations the CTO reviewed and accepted, each with its disposition — they ride in every manifest so a reader of one run's results cannot miss them.

artifacts.description: paths (relative to the run dir) to logs, the built target, and the org's committed artifacts

cost_provenance.description: each cost bucket split into measured vs estimated tokens. A `claude -p` seat reports real usage; a foreign ask-agent seat reports none and is estimated at characters/4. `comparable_across_arms` is true only when a bucket contains no estimate — two arms whose review ladders use different seat types are NOT comparable on coordination_tokens, and this field is how you can tell.

budget_tokens.description: the config's declared budget, recorded so it can be compared against what was spent

budget_overrun.description: tokens spent beyond budget_tokens, or null when no budget was set. Recorded, not enforced: a `claude -p` run cannot be stopped mid-flight.

models_observed.description: the models the BUILD actually used, from the result event's modelUsage — output tokens per model id. The manifest records the configured mix; this records the real one.

models_honoured.description: false when the build used a model the config did not name — a lead that quietly upgraded its workers changes the variable `tiering` exists to isolate. Null when nothing was observed.

swept_commits.description: every point at which the harness committed work the agent left uncommitted, so the reviewed/graded sha names the bytes actually measured

ablation_set.description: every mechanism this regime switches off, named in the config's own vocabulary. Lossless where `ablation` is not: `ablation` holds a name only when EXACTLY one mechanism is off, so r5 (crystal+standup off) and raw report null there while this field still says what was removed. Read together with `toggles`.

models_missing.description: configured models for the build roles that never appear in modelUsage. models_honoured can only see a model from OUTSIDE the configured set, so a lead that upgrades its haiku workers to the sonnet it also uses itself passes it; this catches that from the other side.

study_pin.description: the base sha and input hashes this arm actually ran against, recorded so the six arms can be proved to share a target after the fact. The driver passes the first arm's values to every later arm via --expect-base-sha/--expect-input-hashes, and an arm whose inputs differ REFUSES to run rather than producing a result that is not comparable.
